subject:
Edit this source IMAGE 1 as if changing a level in precisely the same top-down 2D pixel game. KEEP the original low-angle-down orthographic camera, compression of silhouettes, bold almost-black pixel contours, quiet green ground and the dark exposure. KEEP THE CENTRAL RIVERLIGHT EFFECT EXACTLY AS STRONG AS IMAGE 1: a visible vivid cold jade-green light in the water just BEHIND and to the RIGHT of the main round tree at the bend, which spreads into teal and fades to midnight blue within the river. Keep the second smaller turquoise pool under the upside-down lantern in front of the near bank, also falling to navy. The rest of the river is dark navy. These two areas of visibly green and blue water are NOT optional and must NOT be replaced by solid navy water with only a thin pale outline. Retain sparse, soft broken water ripple marks like the image. Keep a thin stepped turquoise edge ONLY near this light. Trees and lamp cast genuine recognizably inverted DARK silhouettes that remain readable in the coloured water; maintain the same soft, clipped lamp reflection.

Make three small local changes, leaving the art everywhere else visually close to Image 1: (1) put a little blue-cloaked adventurer facing the main warm yellow lamp, standing on the flat green bank with a crisp tiny foot shadow; (2) replace the little left sprout with a grey, irregular chipped mossy waystone, with a small warm lit right edge and deep cold left plane; (3) remove the second lamp on the lower right, but KEEP that little opposite headland and its two narrow dark evergreen silhouettes framing the water. Keep the main round tree, directly adjacent to the one bright lamp, partially lit in yellow-green on the side facing it and nearly black overhead. The terrain is restrained, almost flat colour with only tiny breaks, not textured. Shapes are crisp original-scale connected pixel clusters and outlines. No new photographic textures, 3D, tall wall blocks, elevated camera, smooth painting, added sky, loud lime light outside water, UI, border, extra characters, text, or labels. One finished frame, not a comparison sheet.
